 Case management UNHCR’s integrated case management approach in Syria provides individualized and confidential support to children at risk, survivors of gender-based violence, and individuals experiencing mental health and psychosocial distress. Caseworkers follow a structured process that includes assessment, planning, referral, and follow-up, ensuring that interventions are tailored to each person’s needs and circumstances. Child protection case management focuses on engaging children and their caregivers in decisions that prioritize the child’s best interests, while GBV case management applies a survivor-centred approach that respects the survivor’s rights, choices, and dignity. MHPSS case management is embedded across health and protection sectors, offering multi-layered support that ranges from community-based psychosocial care to referrals for specialized mental health services. Together, these services promote safety, recovery, and resilience through coordinated, holistic support. Awareness-raising Awareness-raising is a key strategy in UNHCR’s protection programming, aimed at increasing knowledge, shifting harmful norms, and empowering communities to recognize and respond to protection risks. Child protection awareness sessions focus on children’s rights, the impact of violence and neglect, and the importance of education and positive parenting. GBV awareness activities promote gender equality, challenge discriminatory practices, and inform communities about available services and legal protection. MHPSS awareness efforts address stigma around mental health, promote emotional well-being, and provide practical guidance on managing stress, trauma, and other psychosocial challenges. These sessions are delivered in safe, accessible spaces and are designed to foster inclusive dialogue and community engagement. Explosive Ordnance Risk Education UNHCR, through its 12 partners, conducted explosive ordnance risk education (EORE) awareness sessions across 52 community centres in 14 governorates. These sessions aimed to sensitize communities to the dangers of unexploded ordnance, emphasizing three key safety messages: “Don’t Touch – Move Away – Report.” Participants received illustrated brochures with key messages provided by the United Nations Mine Action Service (UNMAS), ensuring that these life-saving messages remain accessible after the sessions. The initiative reinforces the importance of avoiding hazardous items and reporting them promptly to prevent injuries and save lives. Community engagement UNHCR supports community-based structures that strengthen local capacity to protect and support vulnerable individuals. In child protection, structures such as children’s clubs and child welfare committees empower children and community members to identify risks, advocate for rights, and support peers. GBV programming engages women and men through dedicated committees that promote gender equality, raise awareness, and support survivors in accessing services and opportunities. MHPSS community engagement includes inclusive care programmes for older persons and persons with disabilities, as well as recreational and peer support activities that foster social cohesion and emotional resilience. These initiatives build trust, promote ownership, and ensure that protection responses are rooted in the lived realities of the communities they serve.

The ICRC also endeavours to prevent suffering by promoting and strengthening humanitarian law and universal humanitarian principles. Established in 1863, the ICRC is at the origin of the Geneva Conventions and the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement. It directs and coordinates the international activities conducted by the Movement in armed conflicts and other situations of violence. The escalating attacks threatened to derail efforts to end the war, with Trump warning that Tehran would "pay the price" for stalled negotiations. U.S. Central Command said in a social media post that the military was striking "multiple targets in Iran," attacks that were "in response to Iran's unwarranted and continued aggression." The second day of American strikes came hours after Bahrain, Kuwait and Jordan — all of which host U.S. troops — came under Iranian fire. It was the third time this week that back-and-forth strikes have tested a two-month ceasefire. related.title: Mali: ICRC steps up support to people affected by armed violence
related.summary: Bamako (ICRC) – The security situation has deteriorated in several regions of Mali since 25 April 2026, leading to massive casualties, loss of life and new waves of displacement. ICRC teams are also engaged in confidential, bilateral dialogue with the authorities and parties to the conflict to promote the protection of civilians, health workers and facilities, and public goods essential to people’s survival, such as drinking water and food stocks.
bullets: Bamako (ICRC) – The security situation has deteriorated in several regions of Mali since 25 April 2026, leading to massive casualties, loss of life and new waves of displacement.

ICRC teams are also engaged in confidential, bilateral dialogue with the authorities and parties to the conflict to promote the protection of civilians, health workers and facilities, and public goods essential to people’s survival, such as drinking water and food stocks.

Emergency aid for displaced people: The ICRC and the Mali Red Cross provided household essentials (mats, kitchen utensils, clothing, and more) to 100 families that had been displaced from Korikori to Sevaré in the Mopti region.
“We are deeply concerned about the repercussions of escalating armed violence on civilians,” said Nicolas Lambert, head of the ICRC delegation in Mali.

We are redoubling our efforts to provide emergency aid, ensure access to essential services and strengthen community resilience.” Operational update In May 2026 , the ICRC took the following actions to meet the urgent needs of the most vulnerable while strengthening community capacities and local infrastructure in response to the ongoing crisis.
related.excerpt: Bamako (ICRC) – The security situation has deteriorated in several regions of Mali since 25 April 2026, leading to massive casualties, loss of life and new waves of displacement. The fighting has also put increased pressure on livelihoods and access to essential services. In response, the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) is helping to meet the urgent needs of those affected while maintaining essential services and strengthening community resilience. The organization has provided quality health care to the wounded and distributed everyday necessities to displaced people. ICRC teams are also engaged in confidential, bilateral dialogue with the authorities and parties to the conflict to promote the protection of civilians, health workers and facilities, and public goods essential to people’s survival, such as drinking water and food stocks. “We are deeply concerned about the repercussions of escalating armed violence on civilians,” said Nicolas Lambert, head of the ICRC delegation in Mali. “Civilians are not targets.
